_note: Authored opening sentences for the description sweep (#1404), batch 01.

proposals.current: Creates an RGB image that draws 2D ROIs as colored outlines, fills, and optional labels. It takes a 2D ROI list and an optional reference image; without a reference, it uses a blank RGB canvas. The output is an RGB image of the ROI visualization. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Converts a 2D ROI list into an RGB image that draws each ROI as a colored outline or fill with an optional label. It takes a 2D ROI list and an optional reference image; without a reference, it uses a blank RGB canvas. The output is an RGB image of the ROI visualization.

proposals.current: Extracts properties of the ROI lists and stores them into annotations. This will create a list of annotation values if there are multiple ROI per list, unless you choose the option to only return the first entry. By default, one value per ROI is generated. Enable de-duplication to disable this behavior.
proposals.proposed: Annotates a list with properties of its 2D ROIs (such as area, position or shape measurements) by extracting those values and storing them as annotations. This will create a list of annotation values if there are multiple ROI per list, unless you choose the option to only return the first entry. By default, one value per ROI is generated. Enable de-duplication to disable this behavior.

proposals.current: Copies the phyiscal pixel sizes from the source to the target This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Copies the physical dimensions (pixel and voxel sizes) of a source image to a target image, so both share the same calibration.

proposals.current: Filters the ROI lists by testing for mutual overlap. The ROI1 output contains all ROI1 input ROI that overlap with any of ROI2. The ROI2 output contains all ROI2 input ROI that overlap with a ROI1 ROI. This node is deprecated and was replaced with 'Filter 2D ROI by overlap'. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Keeps only 2D ROIs that mutually overlap between two lists; this is the old variant that has since been replaced. The ROI1 output contains all ROI1 input ROI that overlap with any of ROI2. The ROI2 output contains all ROI2 input ROI that overlap with a ROI1 ROI. This node is deprecated and was replaced with 'Filter 2D ROI by overlap'.

proposals.current: Takes a results table, saves it as a CSV or XLSX file at the selected location, and provides the saved file for later steps. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Exports a results table by saving it as a CSV or XLSX file at the selected location and provides the saved file for later steps.

proposals.current: Keeps only 2D ROIs that match a user-defined expression based on their measured values. It takes a list of 2D ROIs and an optional reference image, calculates the selected measurements for each ROI, and outputs the remaining 2D ROIs. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Filters a list of 2D ROIs by statistics: it measures each ROI and keeps only those whose values match a user-defined expression. It takes a list of 2D ROIs and an optional reference image, calculates the selected measurements for each ROI, and outputs the remaining 2D ROIs.

proposals.current: Implementation of the ImageJ contrast enhancer feature that uses histograms and normalization methods.
proposals.proposed: Enhances image contrast with histogram-based normalization methods, using the ImageJ contrast enhancer feature.

proposals.current: Converts ROI lists to masks. This algorithm needs a reference image that provides the output sizes. If you do not have a reference image, you can use the unreferenced variant. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Converts 2D ROI lists to binary masks. This algorithm needs a reference image that provides the output sizes. If you do not have a reference image, you can use the unreferenced variant.

proposals.current: Applies convolution with a Gaussian function for smoothing. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Smooths images with a Gaussian blur by convolving them with a Gaussian function. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Generates a results table containing ROI statistics. If a reference image is provided, the statistics are calculated for the reference image. Otherwise, an empty reference image is automatically generated. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Extracts statistics for each 2D ROI (such as area, mean intensity or shape measurements) into a results table. If a reference image is provided, the statistics are calculated for the reference image. Otherwise, an empty reference image is automatically generated.

proposals.current: Splits multichannel images into multiple greyscale images. This operation is applied for each 2D image slice.
proposals.proposed: Splits the channels of a multichannel image into separate greyscale images, one per channel. This operation is applied for each 2D image slice.

proposals.current: Applies a Gaussian filter to the image and extracts the maximum value. Pixel values are then divided by this value.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Performs illumination correction by blurring the image with a Gaussian filter, taking the maximum value, and dividing every pixel by it. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Merges multiple stacks that miss a dimension into the target dimension. Requires that all incoming stacks have the same size and that there is only one slice in the created dimension. The type of the output image is determined by consensus bit depth. This node has similar functionality to the 'Combine stacks' node. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Merges stacks into a single hyperstack along a missing dimension (C, Z or T); the output has exactly one slice in the newly created dimension. Requires that all incoming stacks have the same size; the output bit depth is decided by consensus. Similar to the 'Combine stacks' node. Groups incoming data by annotations (multiple items per group); to put all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.

proposals.current: Sets all pixels of the input image to the specified color. If the image is grayscale, the provided color is converted to its equivalent grayscale value. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sets all pixels of the input image to the specified color, either as an RGB value or its grayscale equivalent. If the image is grayscale, the provided color is converted to its equivalent grayscale value.

proposals.current: Merges multiple ROI lists by using data annotations. By default, ROIs with equivalent annotations are put into the same group and merged into one ROI list for each group. Use the parameters to control how groups are created. To merge all incoming ROI lists into just one list, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave the list of annotation columns empty. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Merges 2D ROI lists whose data annotations match, so ROIs from equivalent inputs end up in one list per group. To merge all incoming ROI lists into just one list, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave the list of annotation columns empty. Groups incoming data by annotations (multiple items per group).

proposals.current: Sets properties of all Roi to a user-defined value.
proposals.proposed: Sets the properties of every 2D ROI in the list (such as name, position, stroke color or stroke width) to a user-defined value.

proposals.current: Thresholds HSB images.
proposals.proposed: Thresholds 2D color images manually by setting lower and upper limits for the hue, saturation and brightness channels.

proposals.current: Creates a new blank ImageJ image filled with zero intensity, using the selected width, height, Z, C, and T sizes and pixel type (default 8-bit grayscale). It needs no input image, although optional annotations can be supplied, and outputs the generated image.
proposals.proposed: Creates an empty ImageJ image filled with zero intensity, using the selected width, height, Z, C, and T sizes and pixel type (default 8-bit grayscale). It needs no input image, although optional annotations can be supplied, and outputs the generated image.

proposals.current: Uses expressions to create custom stacks. There are three expressions, one for each Z, channel and frame plane that return numeric indices of slices that should be generated. You can optionally enable to iterate over all incoming slices of the image to generate multiple stacks. If no iteration is enabled (default), each expression is only executed for z=0,c=0,t=0.
proposals.proposed: Reduces and splits a hyperstack into custom stacks via user-written expressions: one for Z, one for channel and one for frame, each returning numeric indices of the planes to keep. You can optionally iterate over all incoming slices of the image to generate multiple stacks. If no iteration is enabled (default), each expression is only executed for z=0,c=0,t=0.

proposals.current: Converts pixel values equal or higher than the given threshold to a ROI. This will create a single ROI that contains holes. If a higher-dimensional image is provided, the operation is applied for each slice.
proposals.proposed: Converts a mask (or any image) into 2D ROI by turning all pixels at or above the given threshold into a ROI. This will create a single ROI that contains holes. If a higher-dimensional image is provided, the operation is applied for each slice.

proposals.current: Generates a LUT from the first to the second color. This does not change the pixel data.
proposals.proposed: Sets a LUT that ramps from the first to the second of the two colors, changing only how the image is displayed. This does not change the pixel data.

proposals.current: Applies convolution with a Gaussian function in 3D space for smoothing. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.
proposals.proposed: Applies a Gaussian blur in 3D space by convolving the volume with a Gaussian function, smoothing along all three axes. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.

proposals.current: Takes a 3D grayscale image of labeled objects and keeps only the labels that satisfy a user-written expression, such as id > 10 AND num_pixels > 50, then outputs the same 3D grayscale image with all other labels removed.
proposals.proposed: Filters labeled objects in a 3D grayscale image by keeping only the labels that satisfy a user-written expression, such as id > 10 AND num_pixels > 50, then outputs the same 3D grayscale image with all other labels removed.

proposals.current: Splits the ROI in a ROI list into individual ROI lists.
proposals.proposed: Splits a 2D ROI list so that every ROI gets its own separate ROI list.

proposals.current: Converts ROI lists to masks. This algorithm does not need a reference image that determines the output size.
proposals.proposed: Converts 2D ROI lists to masks using only the ROIs themselves, without a reference image that determines the output size.

proposals.current: Applies a mathematical operation between two images. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Old implementation that directly uses the one provided by ImageJ. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Applies a mathematical operation between two images with the legacy ImageJ calculator, which runs per 2D slice. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Old implementation that directly uses the one provided by ImageJ. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead.

proposals.current: Applies standard arithmetic and logical operations including, addition, subtraction, division, multiplication, GAMMA, EXP, LOG, SQR, SQRT, ABS, AND, OR, XOR, minimum, maximum, and more. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Performs fast 2D image arithmetics: it applies a standard arithmetic or logical operation to the pixels of the image, including addition, subtraction, division, multiplication, GAMMA, EXP, LOG, SQR, SQRT, ABS, AND, OR, XOR, minimum, maximum, and more.

proposals.current: Applies one of the following operations to all ROI in the list: Convert to closed polygon Convert to polygon Calculate convex hull Convert to bounding rectangle Convert to minimum bounding rectangle (rotated rectangle) Convert to oriented line Convert to fitted circle Convert to fitted ellipse Apply split fitting to polygons
proposals.proposed: Outlines every 2D ROI in the list by converting it to a polygon, hull, box, line, circle or ellipse shape, one operation at a time: Convert to closed polygon Convert to polygon Calculate convex hull Convert to bounding rectangle Convert to minimum bounding rectangle (rotated rectangle) Convert to oriented line Convert to fitted circle Convert to fitted ellipse Apply split fitting to polygons

proposals.current: Converts ROI and an optional reference image into a label image. Each ROI is assigned its own label. Alternatively, the label can be set generated from an expression. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Converts 2D ROI into a label image, where each ROI is assigned its own label unless you generate the label value from an expression. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero.

proposals.current: Extracts various orientation-related features from the input image. These are the same features as produced by the OrientationJ Analysis.
proposals.proposed: Extracts orientation features per pixel from a 2D image, producing the same features as the OrientationJ Analysis.

proposals.current: Converts ROI and an optional reference image into a label image. The label value is provided by mapping the name to a value. If no name mapping is provided for a ROI, a unique label is generated. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Converts 2D ROI into a label image where each label value comes from mapping the ROI name to a value entry. If no name mapping is provided for a ROI, a unique label is generated. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero.

proposals.current: Applies a morphological operation to greyscale images. Following operations are included: Erosion, Dilation, Opening, Closing, White Top Hat, Black Top Hat, Gradient, Laplacian, Internal Gradient, and External Gradient. More information (including examples) can be found at https://imagej.net/MorphoLibJ.html If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel.
proposals.proposed: Applies a 3D morphological operation to greyscale images: Erosion, Dilation, Opening, Closing, White Top Hat, Black Top Hat, Gradient, Laplacian, Internal Gradient, or External Gradient. More information (including examples) can be found at https://imagej.net/MorphoLibJ.html If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel.

proposals.current: Filter that replaces pixel values by the median if they deviate too much from it. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
proposals.proposed: Removes outliers from 2D images by replacing a pixel value with the median of its neighborhood when it deviates too much from it. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

proposals.current: Visualizes a labels image by assigning a color to each label component
proposals.proposed: Converts a labels image into an RGB image for visualization by assigning a color to each label component.

proposals.current: Takes a 2D or 3D ImageJ image and produces a 32-bit grayscale image, where each pixel or voxel is stored as a 32-bit floating-point value. This is useful when later analysis needs more numeric precision than standard 8-bit or 16-bit images.
proposals.proposed: Converts a 2D or 3D ImageJ image into a 32-bit grayscale image, where each pixel or voxel is stored as a 32-bit floating-point value. This is useful when later analysis needs more numeric precision than standard 8-bit or 16-bit images.

proposals.current: Merges multiple ROI lists. The ROI from 'Source' are added to the end of the 'Target' list. Compared to 'Merge ROI lists', this node allows to control the order of the operation. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
proposals.proposed: Merges 2D ROI lists in a defined order: the ROI from 'Source' are added to the end of the 'Target' list. Compared to 'Merge ROI lists', this node allows to control the order of the operation.

proposals.current: Sets properties of all ROI to values extracted from expressions. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Sets the properties of every 2D ROI in the list to values computed by user-written expressions.

proposals.current: Defines a new Z axis and projects the image so that its Z axis is the newly defined one.
proposals.proposed: Reslices an image by defining a new Z axis and projecting the image so that this becomes its Z axis, allowing views through other planes.

proposals.current: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel. Supported operations are SET, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE, GAMMA, MINIMUM, MAXIMUM, LOGICAL OR, LOGICAL AND, and LOGICAL XOR. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead.
proposals.proposed: Applies a mathematical operation with a scalar value to each pixel of a 2D image, using the legacy ImageJ implementation. Supported operations are SET, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE, GAMMA, MINIMUM, MAXIMUM, LOGICAL OR, LOGICAL AND, and LOGICAL XOR. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead.

proposals.current: Performs segmentation via watershed on a 2D or 3D image using flooding simulations. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks. The markers need to be labels, so apply a connected components labeling if you only have masks. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Performs seeded watershed segmentation on a 2D or 3D image, flooding from label markers using flooding simulations on the image. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks. The markers need to be labels, so apply a connected components labeling if you only have masks.

proposals.current: Generates a histogram of the input image. It generates following output columns: value, count.
proposals.proposed: Generates a pixel value histogram of the input image. It generates following output columns: value, count.

proposals.current: Applies logical operations to the input ROI list. The logical operations are applied to the whole list, meaning that an AND operation will create the union of all ROI in the list. If you want to apply the operation only to a sub-set of ROI, preprocess using a ROI splitter algorithm.
proposals.proposed: Combines the 2D ROIs of a list with a logical calculator operation (AND, OR, XOR and related), applied to the whole list at once. The logical operations are applied to the whole list, meaning that an AND operation will create the union of all ROI in the list. If you want to apply the operation only to a sub-set of ROI, preprocess using a ROI splitter algorithm.

proposals.current: Extracts parts of the incoming image within the given ROI by extracting the bounding area. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
proposals.proposed: Extracts the part of the incoming image inside each 2D ROI by cropping its bounding area.

proposals.current: Only passes ROI lists that match the filter criteria.
proposals.proposed: Filters 2D ROI lists, passing on only those lists that match the filter criteria.

proposals.current: Splits ROI that consist of multiple sub-ROI into their individual ROI. Such multi-component ROI are for example generated by the ROI calculator.
proposals.proposed: Splits 2D ROI that consist of multiple sub-ROI into their individual ROI. Such multi-component ROI are for example generated by the ROI calculator.

proposals.current: Extracts the pixel values of an image and puts them into a table. The table always includes columns x, y, z, c, and t. For greyscale images, the value is stored into a column value. For color images, column names depend on the color space.
proposals.proposed: Gets the pixels of an image as a table by extracting every pixel value with its coordinates. The table always includes columns x, y, z, c, and t. For greyscale images, the value is stored into a column value. For color images, column names depend on the color space.

proposals.current: Performs a Z-Projection. This version of the Z-project algorithm wraps around the native ImageJ function and can only handle 3D images. If you have a hyperstack (4D+), use the other Z-project algorithm.
proposals.proposed: Performs a Z-projection, classic flavor, with a wrapper around the native ImageJ function that can only handle 3D images. If you have a hyperstack (4D+), use the other Z-project algorithm.
